newsitem.title: ITALY: New Year fireworks injure 800 in Italy.
newsitem.headline: New Year fireworks injure 800 in Italy.

text.p: An 87-year-old woman was fighting for her life after suffering extensive burns and several people lost hands, fingers or eyes when Italy saw in 1997 with an explosion of fireworks on Wednesday.
Luigia Cattaneo was sleeping at her apartment in the northern city of Milan when a rocket smashed through her bedroom window and set light to the curtains, police said.
The woman suffered burns to 90 percent of her body.
At least seven people had to have hands or fingers amputated after fireworks accidents, including a 15-year-old boy and a boy aged six, hospitals reported.

More than 800 people were injured in fireworks accidents across Italy, 59 of them seriously, according to the Interior Ministry. The Naples area of southern Italy led the accident list, with 160 people hurt.
Italians traditionally see in the New Year with fireworks, often imported or sold illegally.
Police said they had seized more than 30 million illegal fireworks throughout the country in the run-up to the celebrations, some of them containing weapons-grade explosives.
Despite the number of injuries, initial police reports suggested a safer New Year than in 1996, when four Italians were killed in accidents involving fireworks.
